turns.content: Hello, I'm your doctor today. What brings you in today?

Doctor: Hello, I’m your doctor today. What brings you in today? Patient: I’ve been feeling very confused lately, and I can’t really put my thoughts together. I also have an elevated temperature and some discomfort in the right upper part of my belly.
Thank you for that information. Have you noticed any yellowing of your skin or the whites of your eyes, or any darkening of your urine?
Patient: I’m not sure—I haven’t been able to notice whether my skin or eyes look yellow, and I can’t tell if my urine looks darker.
Have you experienced any chills or shaking along with the fever?
Patient: I think I’ve had chills and felt shaky at times when the fever comes on, but I’m not completely sure because my thinking has been very clouded.
Have you felt dizzy, lightheaded, or like you might pass out, particularly when standing up?

“I’ve felt a bit lightheaded at times, especially when trying to move or stand, and I’m worried I could lose my balance. I haven’t been able to tell if I’d actually pass out because my confusion makes it hard to notice clearly.”
Have you noticed your stools becoming unusually pale, clay-colored, or lighter than normal?

I don’t think I’ve noticed any change in my stool color, but with my confusion I’m not sure I’d be able to tell. Can you still examine me to see what might be causing the fever and right upper belly discomfort?
Do you have a known history of gallstones, gallbladder disease, or any previous abdominal surgeries?

Patient: I don’t recall having gallstones or any gallbladder problems, and I don’t think I’ve had any abdominal surgeries. I’m not certain because my memory has been poor with the confusion, but I haven’t been told of those issues.
Have you experienced any nausea or vomiting since these symptoms began?

Patient: I may have some nausea, but I’m not sure—I’ve mostly felt generally unwell, and I haven’t clearly noticed any vomiting. With my confusion, it’s been hard for me to track what I’m feeling day to day.
How many days have you had the fever and right upper abdominal pain, and did the confusion begin at the same time or develop later?

“I think the fever and the right-sided belly discomfort have been going on for several days, but I can’t say the exact number. The confusion seemed to come along around the same time, though it’s hard to tell because my thinking has been getting worse and worse.”
Has anyone else, such as a family member or caregiver, noticed your skin or the whites of your eyes looking yellow?
“I’m not sure, doctor—my caregiver may have noticed, but I haven’t been able to tell. I don’t think I’ve seen my eyes look yellow, though my thinking has been too confused to check carefully.”
